panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E panel of penile verrucous carcinoma tissue explicitly showing hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis, the classic church-spire keratosis component of verrucous carcinoma; disease attribution is certain from the caption and article title. B: H&E panel of penile verrucous carcinoma showing bland, well-differentiated squamous epithelium with little atypia and acanthosis; the low-atypia bland epithelium is a textbook feature of verrucous carcinoma. C: H&E panel showing the hallmark verrucous carcinoma pushing, drumstick/bulbous downgrowth with a sharp, non-infiltrative border; this is the defining 'pushing border' of verrucous carcinoma and attribution is explicit. D: H&E panel of the tumor base showing a bulbous pushing front with mild atypia and prominent lymphocytic infiltrate in the surrounding mesenchyme; both the pushing bulbous border and bland well-differentiated epithelium are classic verrucous carcinoma histology.

Dark skin tone is directly assessable from the image. No ethnicity or age is stated. Findings vocabulary is oral/histology-oriented, so the warty exophytic descriptor is used and plantar-specific features (sinus tracts, keratinous debris, ulceration) are proposed. Plantar verrucous carcinoma is a recognized less common form, hence variant typicality. [raw subtype: plantar]

in_text_mentions: Anatomopathological examination of the surgical material showed that the bladder contained an exophytic tumor measuring 9.5 × 7.5 × 7.0 cm, involving all of the walls (Figure 1). The cuts showed a thick white tumor that infiltrated the entire thickness of the wall and perforated it at the left side. There was no macroscopic infiltration of the prostate, seminal vesicles or urethral stumps, and the resected lymph nodes showed no metastasis.

Histological examination of the bladder showed an infiltrative verrucous carcinoma (pT3b) that involved the tunica muscularis and parts of the perivesical fibroadipose tissue. There were koilocytotic alterations (Figure 1), and the surgical margins did not show signs of neoplasm.
